Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Delegated provisioning for private control plane - initial ask

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this on. We're kicking off our Private Control Plane deployment and need a secure, auditable provisioning flow that lets our identity team continue to manage SAML groups in Okta while letting Redwood translate those groups into fine-grained IAM roles inside our VPC-hosted control plane. Key constraints:
- We must not create individual user accounts in the control plane (only roles/service accounts).
- SCIM must be used for group-to-role provisioning but we need group filtering (only provision groups with prefix "rdw-").
- Audit trail requirements: every role grant must be traceable to the originating SAML group and include timestamp and the Okta user email.

Can you outline a recommended delegated flow (SAML assertion -> SCIM group sync -> role binding) and call out any blockers (token rotation, KMS, service account privileges)? I've attached our SCIM requirements doc. Also copying Laura from our infra team.

Thanks,
Alex Garcia
Platform Ops, Acme Analytics
(attachment: acme_scim_requirements.pdf)

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: ops@acme.example.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-17T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Delegated provisioning for private control plane - initial ask

Alex — thanks for the clear constraints. Quick answer up front: yes, we can support a delegated provisioning flow that preserves your IdP authority and emits role bindings inside the private control plane without creating per-user accounts. High-level proposal below; attached is a short diagram + mapping table.

Proposal (PoC first, then prod):
1) SAML groups in Okta map to SCIM groups (we recommend a stable prefix like rdw- to scope sync).
2) Redwood runs a SCIM agent inside your VPC that performs delta syncs against your Okta SCIM endpoint. The agent writes group membership and group metadata into the private control plane via a short-lived service account token.
3) A provisioning webhook in the control plane translates incoming SCIM group events to IAM role bindings. The mapping (group -> role) is configurable via a YAML file stored in your KMS-backed config store.
4) Audit events: the agent stamps each change with the Okta group id, originating OKTA_USER when available, and the agent request id; these get forwarded to your audit logs and to our Console's token/actor timeline.

Notes / blockers:
- Token rotation: service account tokens for the SCIM agent should be rotated at least daily; we recommend using your KMS to store ephemeral signing keys and Redwood's rotation hook.
- Least privilege: the SCIM agent needs only read access to groups and members, plus a dedicated route to write role bindings (no user creation).
- Network: SCIM agent requires outbound access to Okta and an internal route to the control plane management port (443). We can provide an EKS/VM agent image.

Next step: Marcus and Dev, can you review the proposed agent privileges and the audit metadata we plan to emit? If that looks good, we can schedule a 60-minute PoC kickoff with Acme next week.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: privcp_delegation-proposal_v1.pdf)

Vanessa / team — quick tech notes from runtime/infra perspective (copying forward message for context):

> 1) SCIM agent inside your VPC that performs delta syncs against your Okta SCIM endpoint.
> 2) Agent writes group membership and metadata into the private control plane via a short-lived service account token.

A few items to call out:
- Role mapping file: please use explicit mapping with allow/deny rules; avoid wildcard group -> role mappings to prevent accidental elevation. I'll attach a sample mapping JSON we use in other PoCs.
- Network segmentation: SCIM agent should run in a management subnet with egress NAT to Okta and a TLS-only path to the control plane. Consider mTLS between agent and control plane for additional proof of possession.
- KMS integration: if Acme wants to manage keys in their own KMS, we need a cross-account IAM role for the agent to fetch config. Otherwise we can manage ephemeral keys and rotate via our control plane.
- Caching: to reduce load on Okta, the agent should keep a short-lived local cache (TTL 60s) and perform delta polling.

I'll attach role-mapping-sample.json and a small checklist for mTLS setup.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: role-mapping-sample.json)

From: dev.patel@redwood.com

Date: 2027-04-19T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Delegated provisioning for private control plane - initial ask

Thanks for the proposal — a couple compliance and security points before PoC: 

- SCIM filtering: Acme's ask to only provision groups with prefix rdw- is good; implement server-side filter in the agent so Okta doesn't have to change upstream group names. See attached checklist.
- Audit enrichment: include the full SAML assertion id (if available) in the audit event so we can correlate sign-in->provision events. Also surface the Okta admin who performed group changes in the event metadata.
- Service account hardening: bind the agent token to a short-lived role; require mTLS and IP allowlist of the agent's subnet. If Acme runs the agent in a managed cluster, we should install a pod-security-policy limiting privileges.
- SCIM delta vs full sync: prefer delta sync for production; full sync only for initial backfill.

I'll plan to add these items to the PoC checklist and coordinate with Laura for the deployment runbook.

—Dev Patel
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: scim-filtering-checklist.xlsx)
